# Control Narrative: pH and Dissolved Oxygen Control, Bioreactor BR-500

**Document scope:** 2000 L single-use CHO cell-culture bioreactor BR-500, DeltaV DCS, GMP facility.
**Status:** DRAFT for review. Items marked **[TBD]** are not given in the source information and must be defined by the process/automation owner before OQ protocol approval.

---

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This section describes the automatic control of culture pH and dissolved oxygen (DO) for BR-500. It defines instruments, control strategy, phase behavior, limits, interlocks, alarms and data-recording requirements, each written as a numbered requirement (REQ-x) so it can be traced to OQ test cases.

## 2. Instrument and Equipment List

| Tag | Description | Range / Detail |
|---|---|---|
| AT-501A / AT-501B | pH probes (redundant) | |
| FCV-510 | CO2 sparge flow control valve (acid side) | 0–2 slpm |
| P-520 | Base pump, 1 M sodium carbonate | |
| WT-521 | Load cell, base bag | Totalizes base addition |
| AT-502A / AT-502B | DO probes (redundant) | % air saturation |
| SIC-530 | Agitator speed controller | 80–140 rpm (DO cascade range) |
| FCV-511 | Air sparge control valve | 0–10 slpm |
| FCV-512 | O2 sparge control valve | 0–5 slpm |

## 3. Process Setpoints and Parameters

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| pH setpoint | 7.00 |
| pH deadband | ±0.05 (control band 6.95–7.05) |
| DO setpoint | 40% air saturation |
| Max base addition per batch | 40 L (cumulative, by WT-521) |
| Agitator range under DO control | 80–140 rpm |
| Air sparge range | 0–10 slpm |
| O2 sparge range | 0–5 slpm |
| CO2 sparge range | 0–2 slpm |

Alarm limits, PID tunings, deadband interpretation details, probe-deviation thresholds, and ramp/hold times are **[TBD]** and listed in Section 11.

## 4. Phase Applicability (ISA-88)

**REQ-4.1** pH and DO control shall be active only in the phases Equilibrate, Inoculate and Production.

**REQ-4.2** In Media Fill and Harvest, pH and DO controllers shall be in a non-controlling state, and all associated outputs (FCV-510, P-520, SIC-530 DO demand, FCV-511, FCV-512) shall be at their defined inactive state: valves closed, pump stopped. Agitator behavior in these phases is outside this section **[TBD: defined in agitation narrative]**.

**REQ-4.3** On transition into Equilibrate, controllers shall start and the setpoints defined in Section 3 shall be loaded. On transition out of Production (to Harvest), or on Hold/Abort/Stop, control outputs shall go to the inactive state per REQ-4.2 **[TBD: confirm Hold/Abort behavior]**.

**REQ-4.4** Alarms for pH and DO shall be enabled per phase as in Section 9 and shall not generate nuisance alarms in Media Fill and Harvest.

## 5. pH Control

### 5.1 Measurement and Probe Selection

**REQ-5.1.1** When both AT-501A and AT-501B are healthy, the pH process value (PV) shall be the average of the two.

**REQ-5.1.2** If one probe is bad quality or flagged failed, the PV shall be the remaining healthy probe, and a probe-fault alarm shall be raised identifying the failed probe.

**REQ-5.1.3** If both probes are unhealthy, pH control shall go to a safe state: FCV-510 closed and P-520 stopped, with a high-priority alarm **[TBD: confirm safe state and operator actions]**.

**REQ-5.1.4** A deviation between AT-501A and AT-501B exceeding **[TBD]** for more than **[TBD]** s shall raise a probe-deviation alarm. **[TBD: whether averaging continues or one probe is excluded on deviation.]**

**REQ-5.1.5** "Healthy" shall be defined as good signal quality, within the instrument range, and not flagged by the diagnostics **[TBD: define exact criteria]**.

### 5.2 Control Action

Control is split-range with a deadband around the setpoint.

**REQ-5.2.1** When PV is within the deadband (6.95 to 7.05 at a setpoint of 7.00), both acid and base outputs shall be zero (FCV-510 closed, P-520 off).

**REQ-5.2.2** When PV is above the upper deadband limit (higher than 7.05), the acid side shall act: FCV-510 shall modulate CO2 sparge between 0 and 2 slpm to reduce pH. The base output shall be zero.

**REQ-5.2.3** When PV is below the lower deadband limit (lower than 6.95), the base side shall act: P-520 shall dose 1 M sodium carbonate to raise pH. The acid output shall be zero.

**REQ-5.2.4** Acid and base outputs shall never be active simultaneously.

**REQ-5.2.5** FCV-510 output shall be clamped to 0–2 slpm. **[TBD: P-520 min/max speed or dose rate, and any minimum on/off times.]**

**REQ-5.2.6** Setpoint and deadband shall be configurable parameters with the defaults in Section 3 **[TBD: confirm that the deadband is symmetric about the setpoint, and that PID action starts at the deadband edge versus the setpoint]**.

### 5.3 Base Addition Limit

**REQ-5.3.1** Cumulative base addition shall be calculated from the WT-521 load cell (weight loss of the base bag) and tracked per batch. **[TBD: weight-to-volume conversion, i.e. density of 1 M sodium carbonate, and handling of bag changes or tare.]**

**REQ-5.3.2** The total base addition shall not exceed 40 L per batch. When the cumulative amount reaches 40 L, P-520 shall be stopped and base addition inhibited for the remainder of the batch, and an alarm shall be raised.

**REQ-5.3.3** The inhibit shall persist until the next batch is started; it shall not be resettable by the operator during the batch **[TBD: confirm, or define an authorized override with audit trail]**.

**REQ-5.3.4** A pre-limit warning alarm shall be raised at **[TBD]** L.

**REQ-5.3.5** If WT-521 has bad quality, the system shall raise an alarm and **[TBD: stop base addition, or fall back to a pump-flow-based totalizer]**.

**REQ-5.3.6** The cumulative total shall be reset only at the start of a new batch.

## 6. Dissolved Oxygen Control

### 6.1 Measurement and Probe Selection

**REQ-6.1.1** When both AT-502A and AT-502B are healthy, the DO PV shall be the average of the two **[TBD: confirm averaging, as the source specifies it only for pH]**.

**REQ-6.1.2** If one probe fails, the PV shall be the healthy probe, with a probe-fault alarm.

**REQ-6.1.3** If both fail, DO control shall go to a safe state **[TBD: define the outputs, e.g. hold the last agitator speed and gas flows versus a defined fallback]**, with a high-priority alarm.

**REQ-6.1.4** A probe deviation alarm shall be raised at a limit of **[TBD]**.

### 6.2 Cascade

The DO controller (setpoint 40% air saturation) generates a single demand that is distributed over three actuators in a fixed order. Each stage is used only after the previous stage has reached its maximum.

| Stage | Actuator | Range | Active when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SIC-530 agitator speed | 80 to 140 rpm | First, from low demand |
| 2 | FCV-511 air sparge | 0 to 10 slpm | Agitator at 140 rpm |
| 3 | FCV-512 O2 sparge | 0 to 5 slpm | Air sparge at 10 slpm |

**REQ-6.2.1** When DO is below setpoint, the demand shall increase agitator speed from 80 rpm toward 140 rpm first. Air and O2 flows shall remain at their minimum **[TBD: minimum/baseline flows, e.g. whether air sparge has a nonzero minimum]** until the agitator is at 140 rpm.

**REQ-6.2.2** Only when the agitator is at 140 rpm and DO remains below setpoint shall FCV-511 increase from 0 toward 10 slpm.

**REQ-6.2.3** Only when FCV-511 is at 10 slpm and the agitator at 140 rpm, and DO remains below setpoint, shall FCV-512 increase from 0 toward 5 slpm.

**REQ-6.2.4** When DO is above setpoint, the demand shall decrease in reverse order: O2 sparge reduced to 0 first, then air sparge, then agitator speed toward 80 rpm.

**REQ-6.2.5** Actuator outputs shall be limited to their ranges: SIC-530 80 to 140 rpm, FCV-511 0 to 10 slpm, FCV-512 0 to 5 slpm. The DO cascade shall not command values outside these ranges.

**REQ-6.2.6** Transitions between stages shall be bumpless (no step change in any actuator output when the active stage changes). **[TBD: hysteresis or anti-windup requirements.]**

**REQ-6.2.7** If all three actuators are at maximum and DO remains below the low alarm limit, a DO low alarm shall be raised (see Section 9).

**REQ-6.2.8** Interaction with pH: CO2 sparge (FCV-510) and the gas sparges for DO act independently; no override of one by the other is defined **[TBD: confirm total gas flow limits and whether the sparge flows are summed]**.

## 7. Setpoint Changes and Recording

**REQ-7.1** Setpoints (pH setpoint, pH deadband, DO setpoint) shall be changeable only by authorized users **[TBD: DeltaV security role]**.

**REQ-7.2** Any setpoint change made during the Production phase shall be recorded with: tag/parameter, old value, new value, date and time, user ID, and a reason entered by the user.

**REQ-7.3** The system shall not accept a Production-phase setpoint change until a reason has been entered (mandatory reason field). A change attempted without a reason shall be rejected and the old value retained.

**REQ-7.4** The record shall be stored in the batch record/event journal and be non-editable (audit trail) **[TBD: electronic record/signature requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 / Annex 11, and whether a second-person verification is needed]**.

**REQ-7.5** Setpoint changes in phases other than Production (Equilibrate, Inoculate) are logged by the standard audit trail; the mandatory-reason requirement of REQ-7.3 applies to Production only, as stated by QA **[TBD: confirm that recipe-driven setpoint changes during Production are also recorded]**.

## 8. Interlocks and Safe States (summary)

| ID | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| IL-1 | Phase is not Equilibrate, Inoculate or Production | pH and DO outputs inactive |
| IL-2 | Cumulative base ≥ 40 L | P-520 stopped and inhibited |
| IL-3 | Both pH probes unhealthy | FCV-510 closed, P-520 stopped |
| IL-4 | Both DO probes unhealthy | Safe state **[TBD]** |
| IL-5 | Acid and base demand simultaneously | Not permitted; base inhibited by acid |
| IL-6 | WT-521 bad quality | **[TBD]** |

## 9. Alarms (to be completed)

| Alarm | Limit | Priority | Active phases |
|---|---|---|---|
| pH high / low | **[TBD]** | **[TBD]** | Equilibrate to Production |
| pH probe fault / deviation | per REQ-5.1 | **[TBD]** | Equilibrate to Production |
| DO low / high | **[TBD]** | **[TBD]** | Equilibrate to Production |
| DO probe fault / deviation | per REQ-6.1 | **[TBD]** | Equilibrate to Production |
| Base total pre-limit | **[TBD]** L | **[TBD]** | Equilibrate to Production |
| Base total limit reached | 40 L | **[TBD]** | Equilibrate to Production |
| WT-521 fault | | **[TBD]** | Equilibrate to Production |

## 10. OQ Test Case Derivation Guide

| Test | Requirements | Method (summary) | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| OQ-1 Phase enabling | 4.1–4.4, IL-1 | Step through each phase; observe controller mode and outputs | Active only in Equilibrate/Inoculate/Production; outputs inactive otherwise |
| OQ-2 pH averaging | 5.1.1 | Simulate AT-501A/B at different values | PV is the mean |
| OQ-3 pH probe failure | 5.1.2–5.1.4 | Fail A, then B, then both | Single-probe PV, alarm; both: safe state |
| OQ-4 pH deadband | 5.2.1 | Simulate PV 6.96, 7.00, 7.04 | No acid/base output |
| OQ-5 pH acid action | 5.2.2, 5.2.5 | Simulate PV above 7.05 | FCV-510 modulates within 0–2 slpm; base zero |
| OQ-6 pH base action | 5.2.3 | Simulate PV below 6.95 | P-520 doses; acid zero |
| OQ-7 No simultaneous acid/base | 5.2.4 | Toggle PV across band | Never both active |
| OQ-8 Base limit | 5.3.1–5.3.6 | Simulate WT-521 weight loss to 40 L equivalent | P-520 stops, alarm, inhibit holds, operator cannot reset, resets at new batch |
| OQ-9 WT-521 fault | 5.3.5 | Fail load cell signal | Defined response **[TBD]** |
| OQ-10 DO probe handling | 6.1 | As OQ-2/OQ-3 for AT-502A/B | Per REQ-6.1 |
| OQ-11 Cascade up | 6.2.1–6.2.3, 6.2.5 | Simulate DO below 40% in steps | Order: agitator, then air, then O2; each next stage only after the previous is at max; ranges respected |
| OQ-12 Cascade down | 6.2.4 | Simulate DO above 40% | Reverse order |
| OQ-13 Bumpless transfer | 6.2.6 | Trace outputs at stage transitions | No step changes |
| OQ-14 DO low alarm at full output | 6.2.7 | All actuators at max, DO low | Alarm raised |
| OQ-15 Setpoint change in Production | 7.2–7.4 | Change each setpoint with reason | Record with all fields, audit trail |
| OQ-16 Setpoint change without reason | 7.3 | Attempt change with blank reason | Rejected, old value retained |
| OQ-17 Setpoint change security | 7.1 | Attempt as unauthorized user | Denied |
| OQ-18 Alarms | Section 9 | Trigger each | Correct alarm, priority, phase behavior |

Boundary values (for example PV at exactly 6.95 and 7.05, base total at 39.9, 40.0 and 40.1 L, agitator at 80 and 140 rpm) should be included in the protocol.

## 11. Open Items for the Process/Automation Owner

1. Alarm limits, priorities and delays for pH, DO, probe deviation and base total.
2. PID tunings, anti-windup, and P-520 dose/rate limits.
3. Exact deadband behavior (symmetry, where the control action starts).
4. Safe-state outputs when both DO probes fail, and when WT-521 fails.
5. Whether DO uses averaging with both probes healthy.
6. Minimum/baseline gas flows and total gas flow limits.
7. Base-volume calculation (density), bag change handling, and any authorized override of the 40 L limit.
8. Hold/Abort/Stop behavior of the controllers.
9. Part 11/Annex 11 requirements for the reason record, and whether recipe-driven changes count as setpoint changes.
10. Agitator behavior outside the DO-controlled phases.
